app.title: Mindustry Launcher
main.title: 🎮 Mindustry Launcher
main.profile_frame: Save profile (each profile keeps its own game data)
settings.title: ⚙️ Launcher settings
settings.intro:
"Save profile settings" apply only to the current profile; "Launcher settings" apply to all profiles.
To switch profiles, use the dropdown at the top of the main window.
settings.hint.data_dir: This only changes which folder is used from now on; existing saves are not moved for you.
settings.hint.min_playtime: ← sessions shorter than this are not backed up
settings.hint.max_backups: ← the oldest is deleted beyond this
settings.hint.launcher_update: Only the launcher's own files are replaced - game versions, config, backups and saves are untouched; disabled when running from source
settings.hint.language: ← changes as soon as you click "Save and go back"
settings.hint.jre_path: Either the JRE or the JDK root works (it must contain bin\java.exe); "jre" means the folder next to the launcher
settings.hint.mirror: Prefixed to download URLs for acceleration; empty = direct GitHub. If one mirror fails, the next is tried
settings.hint.mirror_rounds: Each round tests every candidate once. Range 1-{max}; more rounds = steadier but slower
settings.hint.mirror_test: Click Speed test to measure each candidate, then pick the fastest (rankings are indicative when the link is unstable; the result goes into the box above)
settings.hint.gh_auth: Off by default. When ticked and GitHub CLI (gh) is installed and logged in, GitHub requests get authenticated: API quota rises from 60/hour (shared per IP) to 5000/hour. The token stays in memory only; mirrors and custom sources never see it.
settings.hint.extra_vm: Placed before -cp, e.g. -Xmx4G; space-separated - wrap an item in double quotes if it contains spaces
settings.hint.extra_prog: Passed to the game after the main class (rarely needed; mainly for troubleshooting)
settings.hint.max_logs: ← the oldest are dropped beyond this (takes effect on the next launch)
settings.hint.permanent_delete: ← only affects user files such as save folders and old logs
settings.hide_on_launch: Hide the window while the game runs
settings.close_on_exit: Close the launcher when the game exits (after backups finish)
settings.save_game_log: Save game output to logs/ (if off, it is shown live in the log window only)
settings.permanent_delete: Delete files permanently (bypass the recycle bin, cannot be undone)
settings.use_gh_auth: Use GitHub CLI authentication (higher API quota)
settings.game_running: Settings cannot be opened while the game is running
jre.idle: Click "Test" to run java -version and confirm it works
gh_auth.ok: ✅ GitHub CLI login detected, authentication active
gh_auth.not_logged_in: ⚠️ gh found but not logged in: run gh auth login, then come back
gh_auth.missing: GitHub CLI (gh) not found: this option has no effect
gh_auth.off: Off: GitHub requests are sent unauthenticated
mirror_test.title: GitHub mirror speed test
mirror_test.intro: Downloads interleaved samples through each candidate ({rounds} rounds, up to {seconds}s each, ranked by median speed). Select a row, then click Use selected.
mirror_test.need_select: Select a row in the list first
mirror_test.unstable_note: ⚠️ Some candidates varied a lot this run (spread above {x}x) - "fastest" only holds for this run; results may differ later.
mirror_test.none_ok: No candidate passed: try again on another network, or later
mirror_test.applied: ✅ {name} filled in - click Save and go back to apply
reset.title: Confirm reset
reset.body:
Reset the backup policy, global switches and Java path of "{name}" to defaults?
(The data folder, the profile list and existing backups are left alone.)
reset.done: Defaults restored - click "Save and go back" to apply

{err}

Write the full acceleration prefix, e.g. https://ghfast.top/

profiles.intro: Each profile has its own game data directory, backups and backup policy; just switch before launching. ★ marks the profile currently in use.
profiles.need_select: Please select a save profile first
profiles.pick_data_dir: Choose the game data directory for “{name}” (cancel to use the default)
profiles.copy_pick_prompt:
Copy which profile's data to “{name}”?
Everything in that profile's data directory (saves / mods / schematics / settings, etc.) will be copied; files with the same name will be overwritten.
Click “Skip” to copy nothing.
profiles.created: ✅ Created and switched to save profile “{name}”
profiles.change_path_pick: Choose a new game data directory for “{name}”
profiles.dir_missing_open:
{path}

profiles.delete_no_select_body: Please click the save profile you want to delete in the list first.
profiles.delete_last_body:
“{name}” is the only save profile left; deleting it would leave the launcher unusable.

If you only want to clear its game data, check just “Game data directory” in the dialog below.
profiles.delete_running_body: Please close the game before deleting a save profile.
profiles.dst_permanent: permanently delete (bypassing the Recycle Bin, unrecoverable)
profiles.confirm_recycle: move to the Windows Recycle Bin
profiles.delete_hint: Check the items to process as well. Checking everything = removing this profile completely.
profiles.delete_note_permanent:
Note: the data directory will be permanently deleted, bypassing the Recycle Bin and unrecoverable (the “Permanently delete files” option is on in Settings).
Backup records moved to the _trash directory will not be cleaned up automatically.
profiles.item_cfg_detail: Remove “{name}” from config.json so it no longer appears in the launcher's profile list.
profiles.item_data_native_warn: ⚠️ This is the game's native data directory; deleting it wipes your main saves!
profiles.item_data_missing_detail:
{data_dir}
      This directory does not exist; nothing to do.
profiles.nothing_checked_body: No items were checked, so nothing was done.
profiles.orphan_body:
You checked “Profile config” but not “Game data directory”.

After deleting the profile, this directory will be left behind on disk:
{data_dir}

Continue anyway?
profiles.danger_body:
“{name}”'s data directory is Mindustry's native directory:
{data_dir}

Deleting it (even to the Recycle Bin) means the game can no longer find your saves.

Delete it as well?

cli.help_body:
{cmd} {version}

Usage (run this from a console):

  {cmd}                       open the launcher window
  {cmd} --launch <version>     launch a version directly (no launcher window at all)
  {cmd} --list                list the versions on this machine
  {cmd} --list-backups        list the save backups of every profile
  {cmd} --get [<key>]         show the current settings (all of them if no key)
  {cmd} --set <key>=<value> [...]   change settings (writes config.json only;
                              takes effect the next time the launcher starts)
  {cmd} --export <version>     pack a version into a jar (runs with java -jar)
  {cmd} --export-backup <profile> [<timestamp>]
      pack a save backup into a zip (newest if omitted)
  {cmd} --delete-version <version>   delete a version (cannot be undone; needs --yes)
  {cmd} --delete-backup <profile> [<timestamp>]
      delete a save backup (newest if omitted; cannot be undone; needs --yes)
  {cmd} --help                show this text

<version> is the line shown in the version list, e.g. Mindustry v160.7; the bare
version number (v160.7) also works when it belongs to only one type. The name
must be exact — the version decides which save folder is used, so it never
guesses; a wrong name only gets you “not found”.

Whatever --get prints can be copied straight into --set: hide_on_launch,
jvm.jre_path, profile.<name>.max_backups. --set takes several pairs at once
(space separated) and changes none of them if any one is wrong. Numbers have
ranges (mirror rounds 1~3, logs 1~200, …) and out-of-range values are reported
instead of quietly clamped. While the launcher is running, --set is refused: it
writes its in-memory config back on exit and would overwrite the change.

--export / --export-backup also take --out <path> (a file, or an existing
directory); without it the file goes into the current directory. If the name is
already taken it gets a _2 suffix — nothing is ever overwritten.

Deleting cannot be undone: --delete-version / --delete-backup require --yes and
touch nothing without it (exit code 2). Only the manifest reference is removed;
data files are reclaimed once nothing else uses them. While the launcher is
running, deletes are refused (its in-memory lists still point at them).

--launch is windowless: no launcher window ever appears, and progress/results go
to this console. The launcher exits by itself when the game exits. Exit codes
(for %ERRORLEVEL% in scripts):

  0  finished normally (including after playing)
  1  the launcher itself crashed
  2  bad arguments (e.g. --launch with no version name, --set with no key=value)
  3  no such version / no such backup
  4  the version was found but the game would not start
  5  export failed (while packing the jar / zip)
  6  changing the config failed (launcher running / not writable / read-back mismatch)
  7  deleting failed (manifest not removable / still there after read-back / launcher running)

Note: cmd does not wait for GUI programs — the prompt comes back the moment you
press Enter, and it is printed before the program’s output. So trust the last
line, “Launcher exited (exit code N).” To make the prompt wait, put the command
in a .bat file or use start /wait.

One thing at a time: if --help, --list, --list-backups, --get, --set, --export,
--export-backup, --delete-version / --delete-backup and --launch are all given,
only the first in that order is done.
cli.list_empty: No versions yet. Open the launcher to import or download one.
cli.info_failed: Could not read the version list: {err}
cli.bad_usage:
The “{flag}” argument needs a version name after it, so nothing was done.

For example:
    {flag} "Mindustry v146"

The version name is the line shown in the main window's version list.
cli.not_found_status: ❌ The version “{name}” given on the command line was not found; nothing was launched
cli.console_started: Game started in {seconds:.1f}s. The launcher stays in the background; it will back up and exit after you quit the game.
cli.console_no_backup: No automatic backup this time (auto backup is off for this profile, or the playtime threshold was not reached).
cli.bad_usage_backup:
The “{flag}” argument needs a save profile name after it, so nothing was exported.

For example:
    {cmd} {flag} Default

Profile names are the save profiles in Settings (use --list-backups to see which ones have backups).
cli.export_version_start: Packing “{name}” into a jar… (thousands of files, a few seconds)
cli.export_version_done:
Exported “{name}” → {path}
({size:.1f} MB, {seconds:.1f} s). It runs with java -jar as-is.
cli.export_profile_empty: Profile “{name}” has no backups yet, so nothing was exported.
cli.list_backups_footer: Export one with --export-backup <profile> <timestamp> (leave out the timestamp to take the newest one).
cli.get_footer:
Change one: {cmd} --set <key>=<value>    Show one: {cmd} --get <key>
Takes effect the next time the launcher starts.
cli.get_unknown: No such setting “{name}”. Use {cmd} --get to see them all.
cli.set_unknown: No such setting “{name}” (use {cmd} --get), so nothing was changed.
cli.set_bad_pair:
“{token}” must be written as key=value, so nothing was changed.
Quote the whole argument when it contains spaces, e.g.:
    {cmd} --set "extra_vm_args=-Xmx4G -XX:+UseZGC"
cli.set_bad_bool: {name} accepts true / false (also 1/0, yes/no, on/off); got “{value}”.
cli.set_bad_int: {name} takes an integer from {lo} to {hi}; got “{value}”.
cli.set_bad_mirror: {name} takes an http(s) address, or empty for a direct connection; got “{value}”.
cli.set_profile_missing:
No save profile named “{name}”, so nothing was changed.

Existing profiles: {profiles}
cli.set_locked:
The launcher is running, so nothing was changed.

It writes its in-memory config back on exit and would overwrite this change. Close the launcher and run the command again.
(lock file: {path})
You can also change it in the Settings page.
cli.set_lock_unavailable:
Could not take the config lock ({path}): {err}

If the temp folder is not writable, close the launcher and retry; the Settings page works too.
cli.set_verify_failed:
{name} did not read back as written (the file does not hold the new value), so this is treated as a failure.
The file may be locked by another program, the disk may be full, or permissions may be missing.
cli.bad_usage_delete:
Deleting cannot be undone, so nothing was touched.

Add --yes at the end to confirm:
    {cmd} --delete-version <version> --yes
    {cmd} --delete-backup <profile> [<timestamp>] --yes
cli.bad_usage_delete_version:
The --delete-version argument needs a version name after it, so nothing was deleted.

For example:
    {cmd} --delete-version "Mindustry v146" --yes

A version name is the line shown in the version list (see --list).
cli.bad_usage_delete_backup:
The --delete-backup argument needs a profile name after it, so nothing was deleted.

For example:
    {cmd} --delete-backup 默认 --yes

Profile names are the ones in Settings (see --list-backups for which have backups).
cli.delete_two_targets:
One delete per run: --delete-version and --delete-backup given together delete nothing.

Run them as two commands:
    {cmd} --delete-version <version> --yes
    {cmd} --delete-backup <profile> [<timestamp>] --yes
cli.delete_locked:
The launcher is running, so nothing was deleted.

Its in-memory version / backup lists still point at what you asked to delete. Close it first, then run this again.
(lock file: {path})
If you cannot close it, delete from the UI instead (Version manager / Manage backups).
cli.delete_lock_unavailable:
Could not take the delete lock ({path}): {err}

If the temp directory is not writable, try again after closing the launcher; you can also delete from the UI.
cli.delete_version_done: ✅ Deleted the version {name} and reclaimed {removed} unreferenced objects.
cli.delete_backup_done: ✅ Deleted the backup “{desc}” (profile “{profile}”, {stamp}) and reclaimed {removed} unreferenced objects.
cli.delete_backup_done_bare: ✅ Deleted the backup {stamp} (profile “{profile}”) and reclaimed {removed} unreferenced objects.
cli.delete_verify_failed:
The delete command finished, but the manifest is still there: {path}

It is probably held by another program (antivirus, Explorer preview) or not writable. Close whatever holds it and try again.
cli.bad_usage_set:
The “{flag}” argument needs key=value pairs after it, so nothing was changed.

Use {cmd} --get to see the keys and their current values.
